correctness.rationale: The equivariant relative quotient is the wedge of the spoke-link suspensions, with link Ind(P_{n-2}) and a signed stabilizer reflection. The known exact path/cycle recursion yields precisely one nonzero degree; a homotopy-equivalence inclusion proves the first connecting map onto its target, and rational semisimplicity splits the second case. A reduced oriented-simplex Lefschetz identity with a six-periodic path recurrence computes all three scalar signs and then every dihedral character value. An independent exact fixed-face enumeration verifies every element for twelve lengths through twenty; finite computations are not used to prove the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: A direct wheel-matching full-text source gives the known nonequivariant sphere-wedge theorem, while the new theorem computes the full D_n-module for n congruent to 1 or 2 modulo 3 by a signed spoke-relative representation and the rim-line connecting map. Comparisons of objects and implications with cycle matching homology and wheel discrete-Morse complexes show those published results do not already state or imply the asserted wheel ordinary-matching character without additional computations.

value.rationale: Full D_n-equivariant rational homology for a canonical infinite graph family is a structurally motivated refinement of the known 2017 wheel wedge classification. The signed induced spoke module describes every nontrivial rotation and both reflection conjugacy types, and distinguishes rim length eight versus ten on reflection despite equal rank. The residue restriction follows naturally from the noncontractible spoke-link cases, not arbitrary parameter tuning.
